chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, from their father, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Kahmas (and his name is Haytham ibn Ubayd), from a man from the people of Wasit, from our companions, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'My uncle divorced his wife three times, in each purity (period) one divorce.' He said, 'Tell him to have intercourse with her (revive the marriage).'

This report is understood to mean that if he divorced her three times, one divorce in each purity period, without an intervening revocation (marriage revival), because with the revocation the divorce takes effect, as we have previously established.
ai.seo_question: How does Shia jurisprudence determine if three divorces given over three months are final or require a new marriage first?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a man who pronounces three separate divorces across three distinct purity periods without revoking the marriage in between. The Imam instructs that the man must first revive the marriage (through consummation) to reset the count, ensuring the three pronouncements are treated as individual, revocable divorces rather than a final triple divorce. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the intent and procedural accuracy of divorce declarations, distinguishing between immediate triple divorce and sequential single divorces.
